title: Model Capacity Onboarding and Runtime Stability Playbook
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Summary

This playbook defines the standardized steps, configuration templates, SLO contract, and operational guardrails for onboarding a new model or model variant onto the Redwood production inference platform. It targets model engineers, platform operators, and SREs responsible for capacity planning, rollout, and long-term stability.

Scope

- Applies to all hosted and dedicated model variants that will be served through the Redwood inference runtime (not purely experimental sandbox endpoints).
- Covers capacity provisioning, warmup and KV/cache considerations, telemetry and dashboarding, canary/rollout sequences, and operator incident responses.
- Out of scope: model architecture decisions, training pipelines, and private deployment network configuration (see eng-private-deployments docs).

Goals and Acceptance Criteria

1. Predictable token latency at p50/p95/p99 within defined SLOs for the tenant and model class.
2. Capacity budget that matches expected QPS and tail-latency risk with clear burst/fallback policy.
3. Dashboards, alerts, and a documented runbook wired to oncall prior to traffic cutover.
4. Operator-tested rollback and emergency model-swap steps validated in a staging replay.

SLOs and Thresholds (example contract)

- SLO class: interactive-text-generation (small/medium/large model tiers)
- Target p50 latency: <= 35ms (small), <= 70ms (medium), <= 150ms (large)
- Target p95 latency: <= 120ms (small), <= 250ms (medium), <= 700ms (large)
- Error budget: 0.5% errors/month (http 5xx, model crashes, or >5s timeouts)
- Warm-start success rate: >= 98% of warmup requests complete within target latency window
- Cost guard: per-tenant token spend forecast must not exceed 1.25x of requested committed capacity without operator approval

Owner and Contacts

- Model owner: team + primary contact (email) — required in capacity request form below.
- Platform owner: eng-platform/runtime-ops (pager: #platform-operators).
- Escalation path: model owner -> platform owner -> SRE oncall -> CTO/Head of Platform.

Prerequisites (must be completed before requesting capacity)

- Model artifact uploaded to model registry with a versioned tag and inference config.
- Local perf profile: latency vs sequence length, memory footprint, kv-cache behavior, and quantization profile.
- Representative workload replay trace (1–8 hours) in the telemetry fake-traffic bucket.
- Security checklist: data classification, encryption requirements, and customer-supplied keys (if any).

Onboarding Steps (ordered)

1) Capacity request submission
   - Fill the Capacity Request Template (YAML snippet below) and submit at /tickets/platform-capacity with the label "model-onboard".

2) Preflight evaluation (platform ops)
   - Platform to run predictive capacity estimator against replay trace.
   - Validate that kernel/quantization path is supported by runtime (note incompatible operator kernels).
   - Confirm required GPU memory and KV shard estimate.

3) Staging deploy and warmup
   - Deploy model variant to staging region using the stable operator image.
   - Run warmup harness (script: tools/warmup/run_warmup.sh) with sample prompts from the replay trace.
   - Verify KV prefix cache population and cold-kernel invocation ratio < 5% after warmup window.

4) Canary with synthetic and shadow traffic
   - Canary percentage: 1% synthetic traffic, escalate to 5% shadowed (no responses returned to users).
   - Run for minimum 4 hours and verify telemetry thresholds (latency, error rate, memory allocs).

5) Limited production cutover and monitoring
   - 10% real traffic for 2h -> 25% for 6h -> 50% for 12h -> 100% if stable.
   - Operators must be present during first 6 hours of the limited cutover window.

6) Post-cutover validation and tagging
   - Tag the model as "served:stable" in model registry and update the rollout record with metrics snapshot.

7) Hand-off and runbook update
   - Owner must confirm dashboards and runbook links in the model entry and schedule a retrospective within 7 days.

8) Decommission schedule (if experimental)
   - If the model is experimental, schedule automated decommission after 30 days unless extended by owner.

Capacity Request Template (YAML example)

| field | description | example |
|---|---:|---|
| model_name | Registry name and semantic version | my-llm-chatbot:v2.1 |
| model_tier | small|medium|large | medium |
| expected_qps | Average QPS expected in steady state | 18 |
| peak_qps | Short-term 95th percentile QPS | 65 |
| typical_seq_len | Median sequence length (tokens) | 64 |
| kv_cache_enabled | true|false | true |
| required_latency_slo | p95 latency budget in ms | 250 |
| owner_contact | name + email | Priya Desai <priya@redwood.ai> |

Example YAML (pasteable):

---
model_name: my-llm-chatbot:v2.1
model_tier: medium
expected_qps: 18
peak_qps: 65
typical_seq_len: 64
kv_cache_enabled: true
required_latency_slo_ms: 250
owner_contact: "Priya Desai <priya@redwood.ai>"
---

Runtime Stability Checklist (operator acceptance)

- Kernel compatibility validated (float/quantized path tested)
- Batch-size scaling curve produced and safe defaults populated
- KV cache sharding plan created and prefix collision risk assessed
- Memory caps and OOM safeguard set (oom-kill-threshold=0.85 of device memory)
- Circuit breaker thresholds configured (cpu/gpu overload, queue length, runtime error rate)

Telemetry and Dashboards (must exist before 10% cutover)

Required panels and metrics:
- Per-model token throughput (tokens/s) split by route and tenant
- Latency distribution (p50/p95/p99) over 1m/5m/1h windows
- Error rate: http 5xx and runtime-exceptions per 10k requests
- KV cache hit ratio by prefix cohort and node
- Model memory usage and GPU utilization 1m granularity
- Eviction / soft-eviction events and prefetch misses
- Cost run-rate estimate vs committed capacity (per tenant)

Alerting thresholds (example)
- p95 latency > SLO * 1.3 sustained for 15m -> SEV-2 (notify model owner + platform oncall)
- Error rate > 1% for 5m -> SEV-1 if correlated with increased latency or OOMs
- KV cache hit ratio < 60% for model cohort for 30m -> SEV-2; review prefetching policy
- GPU memory pressure > 90% on any node for 5m -> SEV-1; trigger eviction/soft-shrink policy

Canary and Rollout Policy (detailed)

- Canary must be scheduled during low-business-hours window unless otherwise approved.
- Canary progression is automated but requires explicit operator approval at 25% and 50% ramps.
- At each ramp check: latency (p95), error rate, GPU OOM events, and KV behaviour.
- If any SEV-1 alert triggers, immediately revert traffic to previous model variant (automated rollback) and page the SRE channel.

Operator Incident Playbook (short guide)

1. Detection and initial triage
   - Review model-specific dashboards; annotate incident with snapshot of p50/p95/p99 and error traces.

2. Containment
   - If high latency or OOM: reduce routing weight to 0 for the new variant (automated runbook: runbook-scripts/traffic-deweight.sh <variant>)
   - If cache-corruption suspected: trigger read-only fallback (disable KV reads) and assess tail-latency delta.

3. Stabilize and rollback (if needed)
   - If rollback is executed, monitor for regressions on the previous variant for 30 minutes before considering re-try.

4. Postmortem and Remediation
   - Owner to open a postmortem and include: replay trace, operator notes, root cause hypothesis, and list of fixes.

Post-Onboarding Validation and Quality Checks

- Run the model-quality smoke eval suite (LLM-evals reference set) to confirm generation quality at rollout.
- Run cost delta analysis comparing actual token spend to forecast for first 72h.
- Schedule a 1-week retrospective with platform, model owner, and SREs.

Decommission and Version Retirement

- To retire a variant, owner must file a decommission ticket with a 14-day public notice for customers.
- Platform will schedule a dry-run deactivation in staging and then remove variant from routing after confirmation.

Retrospective triggers (automated)

- Any incident that caused automated rollback or SEV-1 within 30 days of onboarding
- Unplanned cost overrun > 30% of forecast in first 7 days
- Model quality regression post-rollout detected by evals

Appendix: Useful commands and links

- Warmup harness: ./tools/warmup/run_warmup.sh --model my-llm-chatbot:v2.1 --trace replay/2024-08-*-trace.json
- Deweight traffic: ./tools/rollouts/deweight.sh --variant my-llm-chatbot:v2.1 --percent 0
- Look up model registry entry: curl -sS https://models.redwood.internal/api/v1/models/my-llm-chatbot:v2.1 | jq
